— three generations, one family
slides.note: Designated a Seoul Future Heritage site in 2013 · Bib Gourmand, MICHELIN Guide Seoul & Busan 2026

items.d: The chunkier version, with the fish left intact in the broth. This is the one Seoul held onto.
Smoother, the fish boiled down and pressed through. The version most of Korea eats today.
Per its MICHELIN Guide listing — so you can taste the difference in one sitting

slides.title:
A soup older than
the border itself
slides.body:
In 1953, during the Korean War ceasefire talks, an interpreter for Kim Il Sung asked whether the restaurant was still around. In 1973 a North Korean delegate asked the same thing. In 1990, North Korean Premier Yon Hyong-muk ate here twice while visiting Seoul.

The original Mugyo-dong building came down in 1960s redevelopment. The family moved about 100 metres to Da-dong and carried on.

items.d: Roughly a 6-minute walk from Gyeongbokgung Station, Exit 2
Saturdays close at 20:00. Per Seoul city's official travel guide, as of August 2026
The older Da-dong room (24-2 Dadong-gil, Jung-gu) prices its bowl a little lower than Seochon — check the one you're heading to
